prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CCOc1ccccc1OC(c1ccccc1)C1CNCCO1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL222

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of [3H]norepinephrine uptake at human NET expressed in MDCK-Net6 cells by scintillation counting
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: MDCK-Net6
  Test type: In vitro

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of norepinephrine uptake at human NET expressed in MDCK-Net6 cells
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: MDCK-Net6
  Test type: In vitro

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.92, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for inhibition of norepinephrine uptake at human NET in the same MDCK-Net6 cell line, with the same in vitro binding/functional setup, same organism, same confidence score, and Assay A simply specifies the radiolabel and detection method (scintillation counting) that Assay B likely also uses, so results should be highly concordant."}
